candidate_relations.rationale: Bootstrap tests proving project bootstrap creates no authority or canonical state strengthen the orchestrator contract's rule that bootstrap creates no operator authority.
The bootstrap no-authority/no-canonical-state tests strengthen the broader bootstrap test record describing minimum-state creation and controlled project identity behavior.
The installer-runner contract's exclusion of mutable heads, network state, time, and implicit version discovery from installed-content inputs strengthens the P8 immutable release baseline.
Authority-grant applyability revalidation before grant-derived approval strengthens the grant-operations runtime's bounded approval/application behavior.
Grant-derived approval revalidation against APPLICABLE proposals strengthens the common mutation substrate's exact-proposal-bound grant-derived approval semantics.

Reconciliation tests requiring activation authority and proving successful reconciliation creates no admission or canonical state strengthen the Steward-authorization contract's independent reconciliation/admission scopes.
The Distiller core's explicit exclusion of `.git`, `.reasoning-distiller`, and `project-knowledge` strengthens the distillation-ingestion operation's exact reserved-root evidence exclusions.

Read-only status tests proving authorization scopes remain independent and evidence presence never asserts semantic validity strengthen the Steward-authorization contract's independent scoped-authority model.
The read-only activation-evidence primitive's rule that activation grants no authority strengthens the Steward-authorization contract's separation of authorization from activation.
Defining package semantic identity as manifest content identity strengthens the P8 release-baseline requirement for exact immutable content identity.
The install-package contract's manifest-based semantic identity strengthens the release-package builder proposition that it constructs a canonical manifest/content identity.
Separating transport SHA-256 from package semantic identity strengthens the P8 release-baseline's distinct transport-digest and content-identity requirements.
The contract's separation of archive transport digest from semantic content identity strengthens the release-package builder's deterministic archive and manifest identity behavior.
The Steward directive's statement that a generic role contract grants no authority strengthens the Steward-authorization contract's rule that registration alone never grants a Steward scope.
The pre-approval revalidation contract's immutable-proposal and fail-closed applicability rules strengthen the common mutation substrate's exact immutable proposal/approval binding.
The orchestrator workflow's composition-only conformance testing strengthens the workflow rule that orchestration intent does not itself grant downstream semantic or admission authority.

The consumer-migration requirement to pin an immutable framework commit while retaining project-owned knowledge and canonical state strengthens the migration record's preservation and decoupling proposition.
The Phase 6 migration PASS record with project-owned canonical state, pinned framework execution, and retired embedded implementation strengthens the consumer-migration proposition.

The common mutation substrate's immutable proposals, exact-proposal approvals, append-only events, and replay projections strengthen the proposition distinguishing direct and grant-derived approvals while binding both to one proposal.
The composition-only orchestrator contract's prohibition on synthesizing authority-sensitive inputs strengthens the workflow rule that workflow intent grants no downstream authority.
Package-builder tests showing semantic changes alter content identity while cache files do not strengthen the release-package builder's canonical content-identity behavior.
The Distiller core's fixed-evidence-only reading and activation-bundle construction strengthen the distillation-ingestion operation's bounded request and activation preparation behavior.
Distiller ingestion tests rejecting reserved roots, symlinks, missing configuration, and overwrite conflicts strengthen the distillation-ingestion operation's fail-closed evidence-selection boundary.
Ingestion tests for reserved roots, symlink rejection, and missing configuration strengthen the Distiller entrypoint's closed ingestion-source selection behavior.
